articles.title: Texas authorities investigate suspicious February disappearance of Nikki Winder | Dateline
articles.summary: Authorities continue to search for Nicole “Nikki” Winder, who was last seen in Brazos County, Texas, in February 2026. Her truck was later found set on fire, and her blood was located at the property where she was last seen.
articles.body: “I wish she was here, and I wish she could experience all the things that life has to offer still,” Colten Winder told “Dateline.” It’s been nearly six months since his mother, 53-year-old Nicole “Nikki” Winder, vanished in Brazos County, Texas, on Feb. 25. Since then, Colten and the rest of Nikki’s family have been searching for answers and holding on to hope they will one day see her again. Nikki Winder grew up in Bryan, Texas, and spent most of her life in Brazos County. Her eldest son, Colten, describes her as a “firecracker.” He says she is loud, fun and always giving back — the kind of person who would “give you the shirt off her back.” He told “Dateline” she regularly invited people who were not family to holiday gatherings, making sure no one spent Christmas or Thanksgiving alone. Colten says Nikki was a devoted mother to him and his younger brother, Coy. He says Nikki had been a single mother since he was 6; she never missed their games and did everything possible to ensure he and Coy had what they needed. Throughout her life, Nikki faced significant health challenges. She had several back surgeries, and during Colten’s senior year of high school, she was diagnosed with renal cell kidney cancer. “She didn’t tell anybody,” Colten said. “She didn’t want to scare us.” His mother has been in remission since 2014. In December, months before she went missing, Nikki was diagnosed again — this time with skin cancer.​ But she “never stopped fighting, never,” Colten said. That same determination now drives Nikki’s family as they continue to search for answers.​ “We’re never gonna stop fighting till we find her and get justice for her,” Colten vowed. Colten says he last spoke to his mom on Feb. 24. The next day, he called her. “She didn’t answer,” he said. He wasn’t worried initially since he figured she may have been busy at work. Nikki worked in home healthcare. “I really didn’t think anything of it,” he said. Later that day, still unable to reach his mom, Colten became increasingly concerned. Then his uncle called and said the Brazos County Sheriff’s Office had reached out about Nikki’s truck, which had been found on fire. Colten says he followed up with the sheriff’s office, which confirmed the information about the truck and informed him that Nikki was nowhere to be found. “They didn’t know any other details,” he said. The next day, the Brazos County Sheriff’s Office posted on its Facebook page asking for help locating Nikki. “Nikki was last seen at approximately 3:00 p.m. on Wednesday, February 25, 2026, in the 19000 block of FM 974 in Brazos County, Texas,” the post states. “At approximately 4:00 p.m., a vehicle on fire was located in the same area and was later confirmed to be Nikki’s vehicle—a white 2025 Chevy truck with black rims.” Authorities believe the fire was arson and the sheriff’s office later shared on Facebook that the vehicle was found on an oil pad site on FM 974 north of Highway 21. On March 1, the sheriff’s office shared an update in Nikki’s case. “Since she was reported missing, search efforts have been conducted every day, and those efforts remain ongoing,” the post reads. They also thanked the nine agencies and organizations that assisted in the searches. On March 5, the sheriff’s office asked residents in the area to check for video or photos from the area where Nikki was last seen. “Even the smallest detail could be important to our investigation,” they wrote. On March 13, authorities released additional information on Facebook, along with key images from security footage. One was Nikki’s truck, and the other was a utility task vehicle (UTV). “We are trying to identify the driver or owner. It is unknown if this vehicle is connected to the case, but the operator may have seen something that could help,” the sheriff’s office wrote. Following the release of that image, investigators gathered additional information about the UTV. On May 8, the sheriff’s office shared a case update requesting the public’s assistance in “locating a 2014 Polaris Ranger XP 900, believed to be connected to the disappearance of Nicole “Nikki” Winder.” They also released footage of the Polaris “traveling on FM 974 at approximately 3:20 PM on February 25, 2026.” The UTV is green, and the last four digits of the VIN are 7827. On May 27, the Brazos County Sheriff’s Office provided another update regarding Nikki’s case, posting that the day after Nikki went missing, investigators “located blood in a driveway around FM 974, on the property where Nikki had last been seen.” Samples of the blood were submitted for forensic testing. “Laboratory results have now confirmed that the blood recovered from that location belongs to Nicole ‘Nikki’ Winder,” the update reads. “The amount of blood recovered reflects a serious injury.” “The circumstances surrounding her disappearance are considered highly suspicious,” the sheriff’s office stated. They shared that they were still investigating the UTV and asked that “anyone who has seen this Polaris being moved, transported, stored, or otherwise observed at any point on or after February 25, 2026, to contact the Sheriff’s Office immediately.” “Dateline” spoke with the Brazos County sheriff’s public information officer, Deputy Nathan Dennis, who shared that the department has searched thousands of acres and numerous properties in connection with her case. They’ve deployed drones, K-9 teams, third-party search organizations, search parties and a helicopter. Those efforts have not located Nikki. On June 17, the Brazos County Sheriff’s Office posted that search warrants had been executed “at two properties in the 19000 block of FM 974” in April, and that the Polaris was “among the items sought.” The UTV was not located during those searches. Deputy Dennis says locating both the Polaris and whoever was driving it is still “very high” on their priority list. They’d like to “be able to put that puzzle piece kind of together” and see if that person had any role in Nikki’s disappearance. “Our investigators are still talking, doing interviews, following up on information that comes in,” Dennis said. Investigators have considered multiple scenarios for what might have happened to Nikki in February. “We can’t say anything’s off the table.” Dennis says the sheriff’s office has not publicly identified a suspect. “Because this remains an active investigation, we cannot discuss whether any particular person has been identified or considered a suspect by investigators,” he said. “I understand that it’s, you know, can be frustrating because there’s not a lot of information that we can share.” The priority remains resolving the case and finding Nikki. “We owe Nikki and her family answers — and our community.” Nikki’s son Colten hopes people continue to talk about his mom and share information about her case. “Don’t stop saying her name,” he said. The family now wears bracelets that say “Justice for Nikki.” Members of the community have also started wearing the bracelets. “Be her voice,” Colten said, “‘cause she doesn’t have a voice anymore.” Nikki is described as 5’7”, 130 lbs., with green eyes and blond hair. She was last seen wearing a dark gray shirt and pink pants. If you have any information about the disappearance of Nikki Winder, please contact the Brazos County Sheriff’s Office at 979-361-4900 or Brazos County Crime Stoppers at 979-775-TIPS (8477). Tips can be submitted anonymously. Crime Stoppers is also offering a $1,000 reward for information that leads to the recovery of the Polaris UTV. articles.title: Coroner positively identifies human remains as those of LaShaunda Spurlock, a South Carolina woman who vanished two years ago
articles.summary: The Marlboro County Coroner’s Office has positively identified human remains found in Bennettsville, South Carolina, in April as those of missing woman LaShaunda Spurlock.
articles.body: It’s been nearly four months since human remains were discovered in Bennettsville, ​​South Carolina. On April 23, the Bennettsville Police Department shared a news release on Facebook saying officers were “actively investigating the discovery of human remains found within a trash receptacle at a local housing apartment.” Police responded to the scene after receiving a report of “suspicious contents inside a trash can.” Four days later, authorities announced they had arrested Luke Douglas Jr., who they “believed to be the last person to have seen” the victim. At the time, the person’s identity had not been positively determined. In announcing the arrest, police said Douglas had “provided information and evidence that led to a confession” in which he “admitted to concealing the victim’s remains by placing the decomposing body in a storage area within the apartment where he resided” before disposing of them. Now, the Chesterfield County Sheriff’s Office has shared an update in the investigation. The office said the Marlboro County Coroner’s Office had positively identified the remains. “The Marlboro County Coroner’s Office has confirmed that the remains have been positively identified as LaShaunda Spurlock, 43, of Chesterfield County,” the sheriff’s office wrote. LaShaunda was last seen outside her home in Society Hill in April 2024. “Dateline” featured her disappearance in its Missing in America digital series in November of that year. Her sister, Tabitha Caudell, told “Dateline” at the time that a neighbor saw LaShaunda getting into a car on April 29. “A neighbor reported seeing her getting into a red older model vehicle, possibly a Kia Soul, on that day around 5:00 to 6:00 p.m. with two men,” Tabitha said. “She hasn’t been seen since.” “For nearly two years, the Spurlock family has lived with uncertainty while holding onto hope and searching for answers,” the Chesterfield County Sheriff’s Office said on Facebook this week. “While this confirmation provides an answer to one of the many questions surrounding LaShaunda’s disappearance, we know this news also brings unimaginable heartbreak to those who love her.” Douglas has been charged with destruction, desecration or removal of human remains and destroying, altering, concealing or tampering with physical evidence or biological material, according to the Marlboro County court website. He has not yet appeared in court. “Dateline” reached out to Douglas’ attorney for comment but has not yet heard back. If you have a story to share with Dateline, please submit it here.

articles.title: Prince Harry and Meghan will move back to the United Kingdom
articles.summary: The couple has lived in California since 2020. King Charles was informed of the move Sunday, a source said.
articles.body: Prince Harry and his family will leave the sunny shores of Southern California and return to the United Kingdom, a source familiar with the couple’s plans said. The Duke of Sussex, 41, and his wife, Meghan, 45, along with their two children, Archie, 7, and Lilibet, 5, have been living in Montecito, an affluent coastal enclave in Santa Barbara County. King Charles was informed of the move on Sunday, a source familiar with the couple’s plans told NBC News. The matter was not discussed during the Sussexes’ visit in July, The Telegraph reported. King Charles welcomes the opportunity to see more of the Sussex family in a private capacity, but maintains that they will remain private individuals and nonworking members of the royal family, the source said. A spokesperson for the couple declined to comment on reasons for the move. The couple took refuge in the Golden State after stepping back from royal duties in 2020. The Telegraph and The Sun were the first to report the move Wednesday evening. The reports said Archie and Lilibet have been enrolled in British schools to start in September, meaning the family will likely move within the next two weeks. Harry and Meghan, however, will not return to royal duties, nor will they live in a royal residence, opting for a more private life. It remains unclear what security — a point of great contention in the past between the prince and the royals — will look like. On the question of Harry and Meghan’s security arrangements, a U.K. Home Office spokesperson said, “It is our long-standing policy not to provide detailed information on those arrangements, as doing so could compromise their integrity and affect individuals’ security.” Meghan is expected to continue to run her lifestyle brand, As Ever, while living in the U.K. The move back across the pond comes on the heels of Harry’s contentious visit to the U.K. in July — where his offer to stay at Buckingham Palace was rescinded and he had to walk back initial plans to travel with his wife and children over security concerns. Prior to July, the Duke and Duchess of Sussex were last together in the U.K. in 2022, for the funeral of Queen Elizabeth II. A royal family reunion may not be a smooth affair given Harry’s strained relationship with his father, King Charles, and elder brother, Prince William, for the past few years. Harry aired some of his grievances in his 2023 memoir “Spare” and has spoken publicly about tensions within the family. Last year, Harry met with his father, who is undergoing treatment for cancer, after he had claimed the monarch refused to speak with him. Despite the frosty relationship, Harry expressed a desire to reconcile with his family in May 2025, noting he did not “know how much longer my father has.” India McTaggart, a royal correspondent at The Telegraph, told NBC News that moving to the U.K. has been a longtime wish of Harry’s. “He’s made, you know, no secret of his intention to want to bring his children here to reunite them with the king, his father, and the Spencer side of the family, and just have a place where he can come to the U.K. without the circus of his arrival,” McTaggart said. She said that while Harry’s relationship with his brother, Prince William, remains fraught as they “haven’t spoken in years,” Harry has “started speaking to the king, his father, a lot more.” Moving back to the U.K. may also be an easier decision for the family given Harry’s charity work there. “A lot of his charities are based here, whether it’s Invictus or WellChild. And I think he feels closer to home here, obviously, because friends are here and I think it’s become so deeply complicated for him to go back and forth because of all the security concerns he had,” McTaggart said. “I just think he has sort of wanted to do this for a while, and it appears that Meghan is taking one for the team.”
